root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `reverse_obs()` indexes `time_units[Q->t_in_id]` in the reverse-time branch, it must establish `Q->t_in_id >= 0`; guarding only `Q->t_out_id` does not protect the indexed table access.
root_cause_criterion.description: The selected root obligation is that the second reverse-time branch must validate the same field it indexes. In the vulnerable original the branch is entered with `(Q->t_in_id, Q->t_out_id) = (-1, 1)`, so the missing `Q->t_in_id >= 0` conjunct leaves the negative array index unguarded.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The fixed original is guarded for the saved PoC because `Q->t_in_id` stays `-1` and the second branch is skipped. The adjacent `with_t_in_decimalyear` perturbation supplies the genuine fixed witness by setting `Q->t_in_id = 1`, after which the protected sink event executes cleanly under the satisfied predicate.

nodes.state: At `time_units[Q->t_in_id].t_out(...)`, the sink still uses `Q->t_in_id == -1` as the table index, so the reverse-time read is a negative-index access.

edges.relation: The same `Q->t_in_id` value left in the constructor is later read as the indexed time-unit id at the reverse-time guard site.
The same `Q->t_out_id` resolved in `PROJECTION(unitconvert)` is the field later tested by the vulnerable reverse-time guard.
The unchecked `Q->t_in_id` value read at the reverse-time guard site is the exact array index used in `time_units[Q->t_in_id]` at the sink.
